#4542. Sykeruns X7 electric dirt bike review: A lot of power for surprisingly little money

The mini electric dirt bike market has exploded over the last few years, with seemingly countless new brands offering everything from pint-sized electric pit bikes to surprisingly powerful off-road machines. The Sykeruns X7 falls somewhere in the middle, offering enough power to get into some serious trouble while keeping the price relatively approachable.

I’ve spent some time now riding the X7, and while it certainly isn’t the most refined electric dirt bike I’ve tested, there’s enough to like about what you’re getting for the money.

In fact, if you’re looking for a reasonably powerful electric dirt bike for recreational trail riding without spending several thousand dollars, this might be worth a closer look.

The Sykeruns X7 is a compact electric dirt bike featuring a 5,500W peak-rated motor, which translates to around 7.4 horsepower. That’s quite a bit of power for a bike at this price point of $1,699, especially considering that many similarly priced electric two-wheelers are significantly less powerful. Oh, and for our readers, we’ve gotten you set up with a 20% discount. Just use code ELECTREK20 to drop the price down to an impressive $1,359!

Sykeruns claims a top speed of 57 mph (92 km/h), though since this is an off-road only bike, you’ll rarely get the chance to put that claim to the test. I certainly didn’t, as I didn’t have a long enough and flat enough stretch of trail where I felt comfortable hitting nearly highway speeds on a low-cost e-moto.

The battery is a 60V 27Ah pack, providing 1,620 Wh of capacity. Sykeruns claims up to 60 miles (96 km) of range, though as with virtually every electric dirt bike, your actual range will depend heavily on how aggressively you’re riding. Fast trail riding, steep climbs, and repeated hard acceleration can eat through battery capacity much more quickly than leisurely cruising. Suffice it to say that you’ll likely not see the 60 mile figure in real world scenarios, but that’s still a fairly large battery.

The bike rolls on a 17-inch front wheel and 14-inch rear wheel, both wrapped in knobby off-road tires. Hydraulic disc brakes handle stopping duties, while an inverted suspension fork and rear monoshock help smooth out the bumps.

At 143 lb (65 kg), the X7 isn’t exactly featherweight, but it’s also far from being a full-size electric motorcycle.

The first thing I was surprised about with the X7 is that it offers a pretty decent amount of performance for the money. There’s enough power here to have some real fun, and the bike doesn’t feel like one of those underpowered mini electric motorcycles that struggles once you get beyond casual neighborhood speeds.

That said, I wouldn’t describe the acceleration as mind-blowing, either. We’re not talking about the kind of explosive power delivery you’d get from a high-end electric dirt bike costing several times as much. Instead, the X7 delivers a healthy amount of acceleration that feels appropriate for a recreational off-road machine.

And let’s be real here, that’s probably what most people shopping in this budget category are looking for.

The suspension is another area where the X7 earns a passing grade without necessarily winning any awards. The front fork and rear shock do their jobs, absorbing the bumps and ruts you’d expect to encounter on typical trails. It’s nothing I’d call plush, but I could see it doing light jumps with minimal air time.

Would I want to take this thing to a motocross track and start launching it off massive jumps? Not particularly. The suspension doesn’t have the premium feel or sophisticated damping of more expensive machines.

But for general trail riding, exploring dirt roads, and the occasional overlanding shenanigans, it’s perfectly serviceable. Not every electric dirt bike needs to be a competition-ready machine, and the X7 seems comfortable occupying that more recreational category.

I was also pleasantly surprised by the tires, which seem well suited to the bike’s intended purpose. The knobby tread offers a reasonable amount of grip for off-road riding, and I didn’t find myself immediately wishing for a tire upgrade.

The overall size is worth mentioning, too. This isn’t a particularly large electric dirt bike, but at my modest 5’7” (170 cm) height, I felt comfortable on it. The riding position didn’t feel overly cramped, and the bike was manageable enough that I didn’t feel like I was wrestling with an oversized machine.

Taller riders might find it a bit more compact than they’d prefer, but for average-height riders, the proportions seem reasonable.

If there’s one area where the X7 reminds you of its budget-friendly $1,699 price tag, it’s the overall level of refinement.

Nothing about the bike struck me as particularly premium. The components, finishes, and general construction are more in line with what I’d expect from a relatively inexpensive electric dirt bike.

But that’s not necessarily a criticism. There’s a difference between something feeling inexpensive and something feeling inadequate, and the X7 generally stays on the acceptable side of that line.

The controls are straightforward, the digital display provides the basic information you need, and the overall package feels focused on delivering usable performance rather than impressing riders with fancy features.

The grippy hydraulic brakes are also a welcome inclusion, especially considering the speeds this bike is capable of reaching. With a machine that can approach highway speeds, having proper motorcycle-style braking hardware is important.

Of course, long-term durability is a separate question. Budget electric dirt bikes don’t always have the same track record, parts availability, or established dealer networks as the more recognizable motorcycle brands. That’s something worth considering before purchasing, particularly if you plan to ride hard or frequently.

One thing I appreciate about the Sykeruns X7 is that the company makes its intended use fairly clear.

There’s a large red warning sticker on the bike explaining that it’s intended for off-road use only. That’s a good thing, especially in today’s market, where the lines between electric bicycles, electric dirt bikes, and electric motorcycles are becoming increasingly blurred, despite laws existing to keep these types of bikes out of the bike lane and off of public roads.

The X7 is absolutely not an electric bicycle. It doesn’t have pedals, it produces several thousand watts of power, and it’s capable of speeds far beyond anything permitted under electric bicycle regulations.

It’s an off-road electric motorcycle, plain and simple.

Interestingly, though, Sykeruns has equipped the bike with features like a tail light and turn signals, which could potentially give some riders the wrong impression.

Those are certainly useful features on a motorcycle, but they don’t magically make a vehicle street legal. Without the necessary certification, registration, and other road-use requirements, the X7 remains an off-road-only machine.

I worry that some buyers might see those lights and assume they can ride the bike around town like a small electric motorcycle. That’s not the case, and it’s important to understand that distinction before buying one.

After spending time with the Sykeruns X7, my biggest takeaway is that this is a reasonably capable electric dirt bike at a pretty compelling price.

It’s not the best electric dirt bike I’ve ever ridden. The suspension is fairly basic, the build quality is unremarkable, and there’s nothing particularly groundbreaking about the design.

But for $1,699 (or $1,359 if you use the code ELECTREK20 to take 20% off!), you’re getting a 5.5 kW peak-rated electric motorcycle with a sizable battery, proper off-road tires, hydraulic brakes, and enough performance to have some genuine fun on the trails.

I wouldn’t say that the X7 here is trying to compete with more up-market electric dirt bikes from the likes of Juiced, Sur-Ron or Talaria on overall refinement, but they make this type of riding much more accessible.

And that’s really where I think the X7 makes the most sense.

If you’re an experienced dirt bike rider looking for a highly refined machine with excellent suspension and premium components, you’ll probably want to keep shopping.

But if you’re someone who wants a fun electric dirt bike for exploring private property, cruising around trails where motorized riding is permitted, or just enjoying some recreational off-road riding without spending a fortune, the Sykeruns X7 offers a pretty reasonable package.

It doesn’t need to be amazing at everything. At this price, being pretty good at most things is already an accomplishment.

#4541. These Vehicles Are Dead for 2027

Pour one out for greats like the BMW Z4, Lexus LC, Toyota GR Supra, and more.

Every year, innocent vehicle models are cast aside and left to die, and this year is no different. With the conclusion of the 2026 model year, more than a dozen different model line will either meet their maker or take a brief dirt nap for the 2027 model year. Scroll down to see the various vehicle lines that won't be available for 2027.

➡️ Skip the lot. Let Car and Driver help you find your next car.

The Acura RDX temporarily calls it quits after 2026. Not to worry, though, a new RDX is in the works. The next-generation RDX is expected to enter the market as a 2028 model, meaning the compact crossover SUV's hiatus ought to last just one model year.

As the last remaining variant of Audi's A7 model line, the Audi RS7 joins the rest of its brethren in the great beyond with the conclusion of the 2026 model year. Those in search of a mid-size Audi liftback will now have to make do with the battery-electric A6 e-tron.

Though BMW calls it quits on the current 8-series after the 2026 model year, the automaker is sure to resurrect the 8-series name in the coming years. Whether a future 8-series retains the coupe, convertible, and sedan (or Gran Coupe in BMW parlance) body styles of today's model is something that only time will tell.

The BMW iX may have never been much of a looker (though it did get a lot less homely for 2026), but it was a great battery-electric luxury SUV thanks to its ample driving range, comfortable ride, and lavish cabin. If that sounds like a compelling combination of character traits, then snap up an iX while you still can, because 2026 marks the last year for the model in the United States before BMW, ahem, pulls the plug.

Consumers in the market for a new roadster have one less option to pick from come 2027, as the BMW Z4 finds itself sleeping with the fishes with the conclusion of the 2026 model year. As the replacement for the Z3, the Z4 spanned three generations and survived in BMW's line for more than two decades. Hopefully, BMW decides to re-enter the reasonably affordable roadster segment in the coming years.

What the Cadillac CT4 lacks in rear seat space and premium interior materials, its chassis more than makes up for. Especially in 10Best-winning CT4-V Blackwing guise. Unlike the forgettable four-cylinder engines of its lesser CT4 kin, the Blackwing's 472-hp twin-turbo V-6 and engaging driving dynamics make it a truly memorable sports sedan. Alas, the entire CT4 line becomes little more than a memory come the start of the 2027 model year.

The Cadillac CT5 is down but not out, as the model's set to make a comeback in the coming years. For now, though, Cadillac shows the mid-size sports sedan the door. Just how long it takes for the next-generation CT5 to arrive is a bit of an open question. It's probably safe to say we'll see the model's return before the decade ends, though. No matter, the bottom line is that the CT5 will not be a member of Cadillac's 2027 lineup.

Though General Motors's support of the current-generation Chevrolet Express and GMC Savana vans extends more than three decades, the automaker is giving up on the battery-electric Chevrolet BrightDrop van after less than half a dozen years. Initially launched as its own brand, the BrightDrop van eventually began donning the bow-tie badge for the 2025 model year. Just two model years later, the BrightDrop finds itself on the wrong side of GM's guillotine.

Though the Chrysler Voyager dies at the end of the 2026 model year, its spirit lives on in the 2027 Chrysler Pacifica LX. Unlike the rest of the Pacifica line, which gets a reworked front end for 2027, the entry-level LX carries over the design cues of the Voyager (and 2017–2020 Pacifica) before it.

Apparently, there's not enough room in Ford showrooms for two compact crossover SUVs. With the demise of the Escape for 2027, the Bronco Sport becomes the Blue Oval's lone competitor in the segment.

Consider this the Prologue's epilogue, as the battery-electric Honda SUV gets laid to rest after 2026.

Jaguar's last remaining model takes a dirt nap come 2027, leaving the brand's model line in limbo until the battery-electric Type 01 enters production.

Like disco, the Land Rover Discovery Sport is dead come 2027. The aging small three-row SUV goes out with a whimper after more than a decade on the market.

MORE ABOUT THE 2026 LAND ROVER DISCOVERY SPORT

Nearly a decade after it went on sale, the Lexus LC remains an absolutely stunning grand touring machine. Alas, 2026 marks the end of the line for the V-8 LC500 coupe and convertible (the gas-electric LC500h ceased production at the end of the 2025 model year). Expect the LC to go down in the annals of Lexus history alongside the likes of the IS F and LFA.

Lexus calls it quits on the model that effectively made the Japanese luxury brand the juggernaut it is today. That's right, the LS flagship sedan is no more come 2027. With this, Lexus's sedan lineup dwindles to just two models: the small IS and the mid-size ES.

Mazda tried to pull a fast one on us with the CX-70. Despite its distinct model name, the CX-70 was little more than a CX-90 sans a third row. The Japanese brand finally got the memo, though, and for 2027 the CX-70 nameplate bites the dust. However, fans of the CX-70 need not worry, because its spirit lives on in the 2027 CX-90 and its available two-row seating configuration.

Though the mid-size battery-electric Mercedes EQE SUV continues into 2027, the EQE sedan, which the automaker sold in both Benz-badged and AMG-badged forms, gets the axe. We don't expect Mercedes to resurrect the EQE moniker on a future sedan, but we wager the hole this lozenge-shaped four-door leaves in the brand’s lineup will eventually be filled by a battery-powered E-class sedan.

The Polestar 4 calls it quits after 2026. Like those seated within its cabin, there's no looking back. That's because the Polestar brand bites the dust. While the vehicle itself may find a home within Volvo's North American lineup, the odds of this seem slim. Still, anything's possible.

For 2027, the only Macan in Porsche’s model line is the battery-powered Macan Electric. The German brand’s gas-powered small crossover SUV finds itself in temporary retirement until the next-generation model arrives at the end of the decade.

Porsche Taycan Cross Turismo and Sport Turismo

Good news. The Porsche Taycan gets a host of improvements for 2027. Bad news. The Taycan wagon (dubbed either Cross Turismo or Sport Turismo, the former being more off-road focused) fails to make it to the 2027 model year.

Toyota and Waymo announced a strategic collaboration 18 months ago, and the two companies have now outlined the next phase of their plan to work together on autonomous robotaxis. The new robotaxis are set to be validated and tested in Japan next year, using the Toyota bZ4X electric crossover (currently known as the Toyota bZ in the United States). The collaboration will mark the first domestically manufactured fully autonomous ride-hailing service in Japan, before the robotaxis are deployed in other major markets.

Toyota and Waymo Strike Partnership to Bring Robotaxi Tech to Personal Cars

Waymo and Toyota’s new partnership aims to materialize Toyota’s zero-traffic-accident vision.

Next year, Toyota and Waymo will conduct testing and validation of the autonomous Toyota bZ4X in Japan. Toyota is a global manufacturing powerhouse, and combining this with Waymo’s expertise in autonomous vehicles could prove to be a formidable combination. The specialized Toyota SUVs will be built at the automaker’s Takaoka plant in Toyota City, Japan. Rather than build the vehicle base and have Waymo install its hardware at another location, everything will take place under one roof.

Toyota’s goal is not only to provide a more convenient means of transportation, especially for those with mobility difficulties, but also to reduce accidents that involve human error. The companies will still work towards enabling autonomous technology for personally-owned Toyota vehicles.

“In areas where Waymo operates, we’ve demonstrated that we are up to 20x safer than human drivers when it comes to serious crash injuries, and our partnership with Toyota will help us bring the safety and convenience of autonomous driving to more people around the world, including key international markets like Japan,” said Dmitri Dolgov, co-CEO of Waymo.

The Toyota bZ4X never got off to the greatest start in the U.S., but the renamed bZ has flourished this year after a series of updates were introduced for the 2026 model year; sales are up by 103.4% in the U.S. this year so far.

The autonomous bZ4X will receive a number of enhancements as it transitions into its role as a robotaxi. According to Toyota, it has been designed for greater comfort and accessibility, with a focus on rear legroom. It will also come with features not found on the regular bZ, such as automatic doors. A power liftgate and special ambient lighting will make ingress/egress more convenient for passengers. Above all, it will adopt Waymo’s leading self-driving tech, which the autonomous company claims has a 93% satisfaction rate.

“Safety technology makes the biggest difference when it reaches as many people as possible,” said Hiroki Nakajima, member of the board of directors and executive vice president of Toyota. “This collaboration will help scale that technology and bring it to customers in Japan and beyond through Waymo’s ride-hailing service, and in parallel, Toyota will continue to explore how integrating vehicles with traffic infrastructure can make those roads safer still.”

After 50 Million Driverless Miles, Waymo’s Crash Numbers Are Hard To Ignore

A recent IIHS study reveals that Waymo autonomous vehicles experience 68% fewer police-reportable crashes than human drivers across major American cities.

Once testing and validation have been completed in Japan, the autonomous Toyota bZ4X fleet is expected to roll out there, before expanding to the United Kingdom, so right-hand-drive markets are being prioritized initially. Other Waymo-serviced markets are expected to come on board in the coming years, but Toyota did not specifically mention when customers in the United States can expect to make use of these self-driving Toyotas.

For most commuters, the most exciting aspect of the Waymo and Toyota partnership will be the planned introduction of autonomous tech into personally-owned vehicles. The idea of a reliable Toyota with a possible Tesla-rivaling self-driving system will be of great interest to many buyers. Lessons learned from the bZ4X robotaxi project are likely to accelerate this possibility in the years ahead.

#4538. Battlefield 6 gets a new map today alongside major changes to controller aim assist, and even more weapon dispersion tweaks

Right on schedule, the latest Battlefield 6 patch has arrived to kick off the next stage of Season 1.

Battlefield 6’s first season has entered its second phase. The game received a major update earlier today, version 1.1.2.0, which delivers a host of changes to the game, many of which have been expected.

The update, of course, also adds new content to the game in the form of the map Eastwood, as well as new hardware and fresh features for the multiplayer sandbox.

We’ve known about the new content side of today’s patch for quite some time. The update kicks off the California Resistance stage of Season 1, which is the second of three. The new Eastwood map takes place in California, and it’s a map cut from the larger Battlefield Redsec battle royale map of Fort Lyndon.

There’s a new limited-time mode called Sabotage - a tactical, 8v8 mode where two teams attempt to destroy as many bomb sites as possible. The other big new feature that arrives today is Battle Pickups.

These are powerful weapons which can be found in specific game modes (and in Portal), scattered around the map for players to pick up and use. They have limited ammo that cannot be replenished, and deliver incredible firepower.

Redsec players have a new Gauntlet mission to look forward to that joins the existing modes. It’s called Rodeo and it involves a lot of vehicular action. Finally, everyone gets to unlock two new weapons: the the DB-12 shotgun, and the M327 Trait revolver sidearm. There’s also a new angled grip attachment.

The fixes and tweaks side of the patch is arguably the more interesting. Controller aim assist has received a big overhaul that essentially resets everything to open beta settings. The goal is to make infantry targeting more consistent.

Controller players actually get the bulk of the changes in this update, which also improves input latency and stick response. Several issues that reset aim assist values, or make it behave erratically, have been addressed.

The conversation around weapon bloom/spread doesn’t look like it’s ever going to end, because Battlefield Studios is yet again tuning gunplay to fix unintended dispersion behaviour, and decrease its intensity across the board.

Certain Challenges have had their description rewritten so their requirements can be better understood. Beyond that, you can expect several deployables to behave much more consistently, including several bug fixes there, too.

Head to the official blog for the full rundown of patch 1.1.2.0.

#4536. BMW is going upscale with its first 3-row EV, the iX7

BMW’s next electric SUV won’t just be bigger. The iX7 will sit at the top of the brand’s EV lineup when it debuts in 2027, bringing a more luxurious option to the mix.

After the new X5 and iX5, the X7, BMW’s biggest SUV, is due for a Neue Klasse overhaul. BMW said the second-generation X7 will arrive in 2027, including the first fully electric version, the iX7.

Ahead of its upcoming debut, camouflaged prototypes have been spotted testing, revealing a few design changes.

Although it won’t fully adopt BMW’s Neue Klasse design, like the iX3, the three-row SUV appears to feature a slimmer, more upright Kidney Grille instead of the traditional wide BMW Grille.

The iX7 also swaps conventional pull-style door handles for small handles on the vehicle’s pillar. It also retains split headlights rather than the updated Neue Klasse-style headlights on the iX3 (shown below on the right).

While BMW has yet to reveal details, a Reddit user who claims to work at BMW’s factory in South Carolina and has seen the second-generation X7 shared a few new details.

Like the X5 and iX5, the new X7 and iX7 will retain a more traditional design rather than going full-on Neue Klasse, including the Kidney Grille. The user also said BMW is dropping the split tailgate, which it did with the new X5, in favor of a standard one-piece tailgate.

Inside, the dashboard and center console are similar to the new X5, but with upgraded tech and features from the new 7 Series sedan.

BMW said the new 7 Series sedan “takes the lead when it comes to the introduction of technologies from the Neue Klasse into existing models.”

Optional features will reportedly include the upgraded 31.3″ 8K BMW Theatre Screen for rear passengers and a 14.6″ BMW Passenger Screen. It will also have optional touch screen panels on the rear doors, the user said.

While most of the claims make sense, we’ll have to wait for BMW to confirm it officially. The new X7 and iX7 are expected to debut in mid-2027.

Like the iX5 60 xDrive, the three-row iX7 is expected to use a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain. The iX5’s AWD setup delivers a combined 578 hp (425 kW) and 593 lb-ft of torque, enabling it to hit 0 to 60 mph in 4.4 seconds.

The iX5 uses a massive 144 kWh battery, which BMW said offers up to 435 miles of range. It will also use an 800V electrical system for fast charging.

BMW showed just how fast it can charge during a media event in Southern California earlier this month, where the iX5 60 xDrive hit a peak of 464 kW. With up to 460 kW peak charging, the iX5 60 xDrive can add up to 170 miles of range in 10 minutes, BMW says.

The new X7 and iX7 are expected to go into production at BMW’s Spartanburg plant in SC in late 2027, joining the new iX5.

Up to 10 inches of snow is forecast above 7,000 feet from Saturday evening into Sunday under a winter weather advisory from the National Weather Service, with higher totals possible above pass level and gusts as high as 35 mph. Forecasters expect slippery roads across the advisory area.

The NWS Pocatello winter weather advisory runs from 8 p.m. ET Saturday to 7 p.m. ET Sunday for the Sun Valley region and the Big Lost Highlands and Copper Basin, including Galena Pass. Ketchum, Sun Valley, Galena and Copper Basin all fall inside it.

Snow is limited to elevations above 7,000 feet, where the office expects 4 to 10 inches, with more above pass level. Pocatello has already extended the advisory once.

State Highway 75 crosses Galena Summit north of Sun Valley, where snowfall is expected to increase above pass level. During one March storm, a slide buried the highway there under snow as deep as 20 feet in places, and Idaho Transportation Department crews worked 31 straight hours to clear it, KTVB reported.

Idaho’s studded tire season opened on Oct. 1. State law bans built-in studs on public highways only from May 1 to Sept. 30, so anyone who has already swapped to studs can run them through this storm. Tires with retractable studs are allowed year-round, as long as the studs retract to the wear bar when not in use, and they may only be deployed between Oct. 1 and April 30.

Chains are permitted at any time, and Idaho also accepts other traction devices if they grip at least as well as chains in the same conditions.

ITD’s winter driving guidance is direct about driver aids. It tells drivers to avoid cruise control, lane-keeping and other auto-pilot features on wet or icy roads, alongside slowing down and leaving more stopping distance, and to brake gently and steer into a skid without overcorrecting.

The department also reminds drivers that bridges and overpasses freeze first and that the safest place near a plow is a comfortable distance behind it. Drivers can check current conditions through the Idaho 511 app or at 511.idaho.gov, a resource NWS Pocatello also recommends in the advisory.

#4534. Waymo adds nearly 250 square miles of robotaxi coverage in 5 cities

Waymo is growing its driverless service area by nearly 250 square miles over the next week, spread across Los Angeles, Nashville, Orlando, San Diego, and the San Francisco Bay Area.

That’s about as big as Tesla’s entire Houston Robotaxi geofence after this week’s expansion, and Waymo is adding it in cities where it already runs with nobody in the driver’s seat.

The company announced the expansion in a short post on its blog today. Here’s what changes in each market, with Waymo’s updated service area maps:

Service now runs down the coast into the South Bay, through Manhattan Beach and Redondo Beach to Torrance.

The zone pushes further south, and riders can now get to the zoo.

Coverage on the east side nearly doubles, and there’s more service downtown.

The service area now stretches north to La Jolla, taking in University City and Clairemont along the way.

Waymo is pushing further into the South Bay, including a connection to BART at Berryessa station in San Jose. The service area now runs from San Francisco down the Peninsula to San Jose and Campbell.

Waymo didn’t break out square mileage by city, and it didn’t say how many vehicles it’s adding to cover the new ground. The updated maps are already in the Waymo app.

Some of these markets are very young. Waymo opened Nashville to public riders in April with a zone of about 60 square miles covering downtown, Midtown, Music Row, and East Nashville. San Diego only went public on September 1, with roughly 50 square miles between the beach and I-15 that barely crossed north of I-8. So getting to La Jolla less than two months later is a big jump.

In May, Waymo pushed its coverage past 1,400 square miles across 11 cities, which is bigger than the state of Rhode Island. Since then, it went driverless in Las Vegas, launched San Diego, and now says it operates in 15 US metros with more than 500,000 paid rides per week. It’s even mapping Toronto for a 2028 launch.

Tesla is also drawing bigger maps. After launching Robotaxi in Dallas and Houston with tiny geofences in April, it stretched Houston to about 254 square miles this week, according to Robotaxi Tracker. But the tracker counts 34 vehicles in Houston.

I'd like to see Waymo add more airports to their service list. Airports are huge drivers of both ride count and revenue for ride services. Waymo currently serves airports in some of their cities, such as Phoenix, San Francisco, and Nashville. However, other major airports such as LAX, Atlanta, and Dallas/Fort Worth do not currently have terminal service even though Waymo operates in those cities. Adding these might not look flashy on a map, but it would be a huge addition to Waymo's bottom line.

And on the metric that reflects actual use, it’s not close. Waymo logged 3.9 million rider-only miles per week in Q2 2026, while Tesla’s driverless fleet did 558,000 miles in its latest reported week, mostly in Austin. That’s about 7x, and it comes on the same day Elon Musk claimed the robotaxi race against Waymo “was never a real contest.”

I like this. Good progress. But I’ll be truly impressed when the Bay Area service area extends south into LA, expands north, and the same happens in San Diego.

It’s going to happen. Waymo is already dabbling with highway operations in California.I can see them linking all those service areas within the next 2 years. Maybe even by the end of next year if all goes well.

#4533. Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with... a questionable selection of maps, but at least the modes are good

If Redsec got you hooked on Battlefield gameplay but you never experienced traditional multiplayer in Battlefield 6, there's an upcoming moment you might want to pay attention to.

Presumably as a way of marching ever forward towards its (alleged) 100 million player goal for Battlefield 6, EA has announced that the multiplayer shooter will be getting its first free trial later this month.

This is, of course, specifically for players to sample the core, paid component of the game, as the recently launched Redsec remains free-to-play. Redsec, however, offers modes like battle royale and Gauntlet, which aren’t quite the traditional Battlefield experience.

The Battlefield 6 trial arrives next Tuesday, November 25. It will run for one week, ending the following Tuesday, December 2. The trial will be available on all platforms, but won’t include all content from the full game.

Instead, players will have access to three of the game’s maps and five of its modes. Siege of Cairo will be there alongside Season 1’s two new maps: Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields. It’s not the strongest line-up of maps, considering Eastwood is already cut from the larger Fort Lyndon battle royale map that Redsec players should be quite familiar with, but it’s something.

As for modes, you can pick from Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch. Battlefield Studios didn’t say what the fifth mode is going to be, but a dedicated blog post with more information is set to arrive next week.

Beyond the trial's content itself, the timing is certainly great. Battlefield 6 just received one of its biggest patches, kicking off the second phase of its first season. So far this season, we’ve seen two new maps, several new weapons - but more importantly, solutions to problems the game’s had since launch, as well as fixes to longstanding bugs.

The miserable XP progression Battlefield 6 launched with is far more tolerable. Challenges and Assignments are much easier to understand and actually finish. The often maligned weapon dispersion has been toned down. Some of the wildest vehicle bugs have been fixed. And Portal has a host of experiences that go beyond just bot farms.

In essence, Battlefield 6 feels like its reached its 1.0 status, which makes this a great entry point for new players, even if the trial could've used more of the game's better maps.

What the press release didn’t confirm is whether the McL 820 will replace the brand’s flagship series-production model, the 750S.

However, that will likely be the case, which makes sense given that the latter is nearing the end of production and is taking final orders. The 750S is a heavily updated version of the 720S, which debuted in 2017 as the successor to the 650S. The Artura, on the other hand, isn’t expected to be discontinued until 2028. McLaren has already shown its capabilities in the hybrid segment with the W1 hypercar, which combines a 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 and an electric motor to produce 1,258 horsepower. Still, the 809-hp output puts the new supercar in the same ballpark as the Ferrari 296 GTB with its 819-hp hybrid V6, Ferrari 12Cilindri with its 819-hp NA V12, and Aston Martin Vanquish with its 824-hp twin-turbo V12.

#4530. Rivian electric van spotted in Walmart+ livery, hinting at a fleet deal

A Rivian electric delivery van wrapped in Walmart+ branding was photographed on a car hauler on I-94 in northwest Indiana today. It’s the first public sign that Walmart could become Rivian’s next big van customer after Amazon.

Neither company has announced a deal. But Walmart’s last two electric van suppliers are out of the business, and Rivian is one of the few companies still building a purpose-built electric delivery van in the US.

Reddit user biggie_ballzzz posted the photo to r/RIVNstock this afternoon, asking if anyone had heard about a partnership. The van is strapped to a multi-car trailer between two Ford pickups, with a big “Walmart+” logo on the side and “Same day. Right to your door.” on the rear doors.

There’s no mistaking the vehicle. It’s Rivian’s Commercial Van, with the same tall body and red light bar wrapping around the rear that you see on Amazon Prime vans everywhere.

A few commenters suspected an AI image, but there’s no clear evidence. In fact, a second commenter then shared a photo of a van in the same livery parked in front of a Walmart Supercenter in Hammond, Indiana, about 30 miles to the west.

Rivian (RIVN) stock was up more than 3% this afternoon as the photo made the rounds, according to screenshots shared in the thread. That’s two days before Rivian reports its Q3 2026 results on Thursday, October 29.

Walmart has been trying to electrify last-mile delivery for years. Its supplier picks haven’t aged well.

In 2022, it signed up to buy 4,500 Canoo vans and put them to work on InHome deliveries. Canoo filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in January 2025 and ceased operations.

The same year, Walmart reserved 5,000 BrightDrop vans from GM, and officially added them to its delivery fleet in late 2024. Then GM killed BrightDrop production at its CAMI plant in Ontario a year ago, with no plan to build the van anywhere else. BrightDrop was on pace for roughly 4,000 US sales in 2025, compared to more than 60,000 for GM’s gas-powered Express and Savana vans.

So Walmart is running two orphaned EV van platforms. And if it wants more purpose-built electric vans at scale, the list of US options is very short.

Amazon ordered 100,000 vans from Rivian, and its fleet has now passed 40,000 units on the road. But the deal came with an exclusivity period that ended in November 2023, and Rivian has struggled to land anything close to Amazon-scale since.

AT&T signed up for a pilot in late 2023, and HelloFresh came on board in 2025. In February 2025, Rivian opened van sales to any business, with the RCV 500 starting at $79,900 and the larger RCV 700 at $83,900. None of those customers moves the needle like Walmart would.

There’s also a charging angle. Walmart now operates its own 400 kW fast-charging network at 100 stores in 20 states, and its manager of retail charging, Wade Higgins, previously worked at Rivian, according to his bio on the board of Minnesota car-sharing nonprofit HOURCAR.

One van on a trailer isn’t a fleet order. Not yet, anyway. This could be a test unit for a pilot program, like the one AT&T announced in 2023. And since Rivian sells vans to any business now, Walmart could have simply bought a few to try them out.

So Walmart is running two orphaned EV van platforms. And if it wants more purpose-built electric vans at scale, the list of US options is very short.

Walmart also runs Ford E-Transit vans but I can't find recent numbers for how many

But the timing makes sense. Walmart bet on Canoo and GM, and both left it with vans nobody builds anymore. If you’re Walmart and you want to keep electrifying same-day delivery, Rivian is the obvious call. Its plant in Normal, Illinois, has already built tens of thousands of these vans, and the platform has been proven at scale by the one company Walmart is trying to beat on delivery.

That’s the awkward part. Walmart putting its brand on the same van as Amazon Prime is a bit funny, and it says a lot about how thin the electric van market has gotten in the US.

For Rivian, a Walmart deal would matter. The van business gives it volume in Normal while R2 ramps, and it badly needs proof that the van isn’t just an Amazon product. We’ll see if Rivian says anything on Thursday’s call. We wouldn’t bet on a massive order announcement, but a Walmart pilot wouldn’t surprise us one bit.

Rivian’s new midsize crossover performed well despite a high starting price. For now, the model starts at $59,485 for the R2 Performance with the Launch Package, but that hasn’t stopped customers from purchasing it anyway.

The rest of the lineup will follow in the near future. The Rivian R2 Performance, the sole trim since June this year, is the top-of-the-line variant, and it will eventually be joined by a mid-grade Premium and a base model that’ll only cost $46,485.

Since June of this year, Rivian has noted that the demand for the R2 was pretty strong, and “reservation and conversion rates for the launch edition R2 remained higher in the quarter than our expectations,” said Rivian’s CEO, RJ Scaringe.

Now that the third quarter is finished, the company has since reported in its earnings call on October 29, 2026, that it outsold the bigger and more expensive R1S crossover and R1T pickup truck combined, becoming Rivian’s top-selling model in the quarter for the U.S. and Canada, while also beating out its sales for its electric delivery vans for Amazon.

The result can be attributed to how Rivian went about selling the R2. The brand raised its overall 2026 delivery guidance to between 67,000 and 70,000 vehicles. Previous delivery guidance was set between 65,000 and 70,000. Rivian also stated that it recently added a second shift at its Normal, Illinois, factory for the initial sales.

The R2 Performance launching first was no accident. Rivian stated that it’s “been able to very intentionally sequence the nature of launching with a high-price variant and then bringing in these other trims as our volume grows, such that in the end it supports a healthy, positive gross margin for the R2 business.”

High-end variants are usually where brands make the most money. With the R2 Performance, each sale returns a good margin back to Rivian for every car sold. When Rivian is ready to unleash its more affordable trims, it can potentially maintain the model’s sales momentum.

The R2 was well-received by the industry, and reviewers have praised it so far, along with a bit of controversy in tow. With 656 horsepower from a dual motor, all-wheel-drive, and a zero-to-sixty time of 3.6 seconds, it’s a rather exciting crossover. Couple that with a range of 330 miles, plus fast charging from 10% to 80% in under 30 minutes, and you have an EV that’s worthy of being a daily driver.

On top of that, the launch edition of the R2 comes with a lifetime Autonomy Plus driver-assistance subscription and a unique key fob in green, and an optional green exterior color and tow package.

With that being said, Rivian needs to strike while the iron is still hot and can’t wait too long to launch its more affordable trims. The R2 Performance starts at $59,485 and can go up from there.

Meanwhile, Rivian’s Premium trim, the mid-grade variant, will start at $55,485 (with shipping) and will come in “late 2026,” according to Rivian’s website. The midrange trim will come with 450 horsepower, all-wheel drive, and 330 miles of range. At the base model trim, the R2 Standard will start at $46,485 and come with 275 miles of range and be available as a rear-wheel-drive powertrain only. This model is expected to launch in summer 2027, according to Rivian.

Customers who want the base model will still be able to spec it out in case they want more capability. The long-range version will cost $3,500 more, but customers may also get long-range and all-wheel drive for $7,000.

Regular prices start at 65,900 yuan ($9,900), which is still less than its predecessor. The first-generation Seagull EV started at 69,900 yuan ($10,500) without incentives, making it BYD’s most affordable purely electric vehicle in China.

For its second generation, the Seagull is bigger, more advanced, and adds a bit more luxury to the entry-level segment.

The new BYD Seagull is 4,205 mm long, 1,810 mm wide, and 1,570 mm high, with a 2,650 mm wheelbase. That’s 425 mm longer and has a 150 mm longer wheelbase than the previous model.

Thanks to the added space, BYD’s electric hatch now offers room for five passengers, up from four seats that the first-gen Seagull had.

The new Seagull uses BYD’s Blade Batteries 2.0 and Flash Charging Technology. As such, the battery can charge from 10% to 70% in five minutes. A full recharge, or 10% to 97%, takes just nine minutes. Even in temperatures as low as -30°C, it takes 12 minutes to charge from 20% to 97%.

It’s available with two LFP battery packs: 30.1 kWh and 39.2 kWh, providing CLTC ranges of 320 km (199 miles) and 420 km (261 miles), respectively.

To improve the ride quality and handling, BYD upgraded the rear suspension to a multi-link independent system.

#4527. Battlefield 6 streamlines some of the most annoying Challenges yet again, takes out a few of them entirely

The easier and more accessible Battlefield Studios makes those Battlefield 6 Challenges, the better.

The work to continue streamlining Challenges in Battlefield 6 is clearly not done. Having just released a new patch - which already included several updates to Challenges and Assignments - Battlefield Studios has gone in and made even more changes.

This latest round includes far fewer tweaks, but quite surprisingly, it also removes a few of the more annoying ones from the game.

The updated list, which Battlefield shared on Twitter, includes changes to the dreaded Recon 2 headshots beyond 150m Challenge. Now, any headshot beyond 75m will count. Recon Expert 3 is another headshot-themed one that’s been updated, and now requires getting headshot kills beyond 125m, rather than the practically impossible beyond 200m that it required previously.

The Rapid Fire 2 Challenge, which required getting kills beyond 50m with Assault Rifles, has been changed so it now tracks anything beyond 40m. The painful ‘Inflict damage under 15m while hip-firing with Assault Rifles’ has been entirely replaced with one that requires - the far more sensible - inflicting damage while in ADS with Assault Rifles.

A couple of Challenges, such as the one that required suppressing enemies with LMGs, and another that wanted you to deal damage to laser-designated vehicles using lock-on weapons, have both been removed.

The journey to make Challenges and Assignments easier to complete has been a long one. Progression has been one of the key areas of criticism Battlefield 6 received at launch. The issue encompassed more than just slow player and weapon XP earn rates, it also prevented players from accessing new Training Paths for the various classes, and several of the game's weapons.

Battlefield Studios attacked the problem from multiple angles, initially boosting the XP players and their weapons would earn, before later reducing the requirements of the Challenges themselves. The developer continued to streamline those requirements over multiple patches, including majorly overhauling the system earlier this month.

It seems the studio is more confident than ever in the game, as it recently announced that Battlefield 6 will be getting its first free trial next week, offering players who do not own the full game access to iconic modes like Conquest, and Breakthrough - though on an unusual selection of maps.

But we can’t be sure – these are placeholder headlight and taillight units, as is common when a prototype ventures into the wild for the first time. Thus, BMW may well be doing something completely unpredictable with the front of new or facelifted M cars like the X5 M and M5, respectively. Now for the elephant in the room: this is the electric X5 M (it won’t be called iX5 M), one of 30 new M models coming by 2029, and like the impending electric M3 (not iM3 either) teased earlier this month, it appears to be gaining vents in the hood, helping cool the front motors of the 800-volt quad-motor powertrain.

It also appears that the hood of this X5 M prototype doesn’t have as deep a recess in the center as other Neue Klasse designs, perhaps as another way of making the X5 M look more brutish than 3 Series-based M models. Then again, if the front fascia is not set in stone, the hood shape may change too, and the above video suggests there’s some subtle cladding on this bodywork. Whatever the case, the bumpers seem to hang over the front and rear ends a little more than normal, and at the back, a jagged dual-element spoiler with a large central recess adds to the angry look. In profile, drilled brake discs provide another hint that this is the M version, though these wheels won’t make production. A glass roof also appears to be visible, and inside, we can expect the upholstery and the Panoramic Vision iDrive system to get M-specific graphics and motifs.

Expected to enter production at BMW’s Spartanburg plant in South Carolina in 2028, the G95 BMW X5 M is predicted to arrive eight months before the gas-powered X5 enters production in December 2028, meaning the V8 version could only launch in 2029. To help sell the EV, which will undoubtedly be heavier and more controversial, the electric X5 M is rumored to make up to 900 horsepower, according to BMW Blog. That explains the meaty new Michelin Pilot Sport S 5 rubber we’ve seen before, but what about the gas X5 M? Well, the current X5 M Competition (a badge that will soon disappear) makes 617 horsepower. As a mild hybrid, it’s far less powerful than the M5 with which it shares a 4.4-liter V8, but perhaps the M Division will put a big battery in the SUV too. Perhaps it will find other ways to increase the S68’s efficiency and performance, possibly including timing, ignition, and turbocharger improvements. Either way, expect a significant leap in output, potentially near the 700-hp mark.

#4525. Renewables to reach 40% of total generating capacity, beat gas within a year – EIA

Over the coming year, renewables’ share of total generating capacity will grow from 37.7% to 40.4%, surpassing that of natural gas and outstripping nuclear capacity fivefold, according to new data released by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) and reviewed by the SUN DAY Campaign.

According to the EIA’s latest “Electric Power Monthly” report (with data through August 31, 2026), renewably generated electricity during the first two-thirds of 2026 was 10.2% greater year over year. The growth was led by utility-scale [>1 MW] solar (up 20.0%), small-scale solar (up 12.0%), wind (up 7.8%), hydropower (up 4.2%), and geothermal (up 3.8%).

From January to August 2026, wind produced 333,367 gigawatt-hours (GWh) – 10.6% of total US electrical generation – while utility-scale and small-scale solar combined produced 329,119 GWh (10.5%), hydropower produced 180,940 GWh (5.7%), biomass produced 29,917 GWh (1.0%), and geothermal produced 10,766 GWh (0.34%).

By comparison, the electrical output of US natural gas and nuclear power plants grew more slowly – by just 2.6% and 1.3%, respectively. Electricity produced by US coal plants fell by 8.7%.

During the first eight months of 2026, the combination of wind and solar, including small-scale solar, accounted for almost 21.1% of domestic electricity production, with wind at 10.6% and solar at nearly 10.5%.

During the first two-thirds of this year, wind and solar combined produced 44.4% more electricity than coal and 24.8% more than nuclear.

Through the end of August, the mix of all renewables, including biomass, accounted for 28.1% of total US electrical generation – up from 26.2% a year earlier.

Between September 1, 2025, and August 31, 2026, the installed capacity of utility-scale solar increased by 27,141.7 MW, while that of small-scale solar and wind grew by 6,526.1 MW and 9,979.1 MW (including 800 MW of offshore wind), respectively. The combined capacity of all renewable energy sources, including hydropower, biomass, and geothermal, expanded by 43,497.9 MW.

In addition, utility-scale battery energy storage capacity increased by 17,586.9 MW.

By comparison, coal capacity fell by 2,703.4 MW, while nuclear capacity remained unchanged. However, natural gas capacity rose by 5,316.0 MW. Combined, net new nuclear and fossil fuel capacity totaled just 2,612.6 MW.

Thus, renewable energy’s capacity expansion was nearly 17 times greater than the net growth of fossil fuels and nuclear power combined.

The EIA projects that the rapid growth of renewables over the past year will accelerate in the coming year.

As of September 1, 2026, renewable energy’s share of total US utility-scale generating capacity was 34.5%. EIA projects this to grow to 37.3% by August 31, 2027. Utility-scale solar will add 44,603.1 MW, thereby expanding its share from 13.4% to 16.5%, while wind will grow by 8,312.3 MW (including 3,355.0 MW of offshore wind), increasing from 13.4% to 13.5%. The mix of other renewables (hydropower, biomass, and geothermal) will add 201.9 MW.

The combined net capacity growth of all utility-scale renewable energy sources over the 12-month period (53,117.3 MW) is almost 44% higher than that added over the previous 12 months (36,971.8 MW). It would bring renewables’ share of total US utility-scale generating capacity up to 37.3%.

Meanwhile, EIA projects no new nuclear generating capacity and a net decline of 1,997.0 MW in fossil fuel capacity.

The figures cited above don’t include small-scale solar. The estimated capacity of small-scale solar systems grew by 6,526.1 MW during the last year, bringing its total to 63,192.6 MW. EIA does not provide a forecast for small-scale solar capacity growth over the next 12 months, but the SUN DAY Campaign assumes it will roughly equal the 6,400 MW added on average over each of the past five years. Therefore, it is conservatively assumed that an additional 6,000 MW or more will come online in the coming year.

If small-scale solar increases by approximately 6,000 MW by September 1, 2027, it will bring renewable energy’s installed capacity to about 550,000 MW. By comparison, natural gas’ projected generating capacity would total 518,312.8 MW.

Solar power’s share alone would be more than one-fifth (20.7%) of total US generating capacity.

EIA foresees battery energy storage adding another 23,656.2 MW by September 1, 2027 – an increase of 43.7%, bringing the total up to 77,753.2 MW.

Thus, the combination of utility-scale renewable energy sources and battery energy storage will provide 76,773.5 MW of new clean energy capacity by late summer 2027. With the inclusion of small-scale solar, that figure could rise to 82.8 GW of new generating capacity.

Google CAISO to see what percent of the California grid is supplied by renewable energy on each and every day, typically more than 70% and often 100%., And they have 16 GW of battery storage, providing renewable electricity 24 seven to the California electrical grid.

“Each new issue of EIA’s ‘Electric Power Monthly’ reinforces the theme that the growth of solar, wind, and battery storage has become unstoppable,” noted the SUN DAY Campaign’s executive director Ken Bossong. “Meanwhile, the share of the nation’s electrical generation and generating capacity provided by fossil fuels and nuclear continues to shrink.”

A 21-year-old Washington driver learned a harsh lesson after crashing his Porsche 911 GT3 during a 127-mph police chase and begging to get the sports car back.

Ferrari Challenge Stradale Is Reportedly Returning After 20-Plus Years

Aston Martin Has Lost $3.1 Billion Since Stroll Took Over

If you ever find yourself running from the cops in a high-performance German sports car, it is probably best not to ask for the vehicle back once you are finally in handcuffs. A 21-year-old driver in Everett, Washington, learned this lesson the hard way after leading police on a wild, high-speed pursuit. The driver, identified as Tyger S. Yong, was behind the wheel of a bright blue 2014 Porsche 911 GT3 when a Snohomish County sheriff’s deputy clocked him traveling at a blistering 127 mph near Interstate 5.

Rather than pulling over, the driver allegedly attempted to outrun law enforcement. While we frequently see stories regarding teens fleeing police in stolen muscle cars, doing so in a highly recognizable, track-focused Porsche is a uniquely terrible idea. The chase eventually came to an abrupt halt when deputies successfully deployed spike strips, destroying both of the GT3’s passenger-side tires and forcing the expensive sports car to a complete stop in traffic.

According to a report from Road & Track, bodycam footage released by the sheriff’s office captured the immediate aftermath of the arrest, providing a brutally honest exchange between the suspect and the arresting deputy. When confronted about why he continued speeding, Yong reportedly claimed he was simply trying to get home. The deputy immediately dismissed the excuse, stating that the suspect was clearly trying to escape.

The situation became even more surreal when Yong asked if there was anything he could do to get his car back. The deputy delivered a deadpan, reality-checking response: “Not run from the police,” before explicitly warning the young driver that his prized sports car would likely end up belonging to the sheriff’s office. To make matters worse, Yong’s wife was riding in the passenger seat during the 127 mph pursuit, leading deputies to refer a domestic-violence-designated reckless endangerment allegation due to the severe risk of injury.

Watching a beautifully engineered 911 GT3 get impounded is always a painful sight for any enthusiast. While the manufacturer is currently relying on high-margin models to boost its profits and continues finding ways to make its highly allocated track cars even more exclusive, this specific GT3 is permanently off the consumer market.

The Snohomish County Sheriff’s Office currently has official possession of the 2014 Porsche and is actively pursuing its legal seizure under state laws regarding vehicles used in felony eluding. Ultimately, this high-speed stunt serves as an incredibly expensive reminder that attempting to outrun a police radio will almost always result in losing your license, your freedom, and your dream car.

#4522. Arc Raiders patch nerfs the Deadline mine, ends the menace of the Venator

The first post-Stella Montis patch for Arc Raiders has arrived, and it predictably touches much of what people brought to the latest map.

Arc Raiders has received a new update today that’s almost entirely dedicated to balance and economy tweaks. Patch 1.3.0 arrived earlier across all platforms, coming in at just under 1GB. This is an especially interesting patch because many of the changes it makes can be seen as a response to player behaviour on Stella Montis, the game’s latest map, which just joined the roster last week.

Stella Montis is available for players who’ve put in a decent number of rounds, and its close-quarters, enclosed environments have essentially turned it into the new “PvP map”, where constant action can be found.

That, of course, also means that the map has exposed a few balance issues with some of the game’s weapons and tools. Case in point: the Venator, a pistol that saw a lot of use recently. The weapon is especially powerful when fully-upgraded, something Arc Raiders developer Embark said pushed it beyond what had been originally intended.

In today’s update, the Venator's fire rate is the thing getting hit the hardest, with each upgrade now offering slower gains to the weapon's rate-of-fire compared to the way things were. The weapon’s weight is also being increased to five from two.

Another powerful item players have been getting a lot of mileage out of recently has been the Deadline mine. Unlike the Venator, the Deadline is mainly a threat to Arc enemies, and it’s proven incredibly powerful against the largest and most fearsome, such as the Bastion, and Leaper. In fact, the mine was considered essential when taking down a Queen.

The patch vastly increases its purchase price, and makes it more difficult to craft by upping the amount each of its components requires. Perhaps the most effective nerf, however, is the reduction to the Deadline’s stock at traders from three to just one, which means you’re going to be seeing a lot less of it topside.

Beyond those specific changes, Embark has also tweaked explosive damage across the board. According to the developer, explosive damage was being applied to multiple parts at once, which trivialised some encounters.

This change mainly affects larger Arc units, such as the Bastion, allowing them to withstand more explosive damage before bits start coming off of them. The Hullcracker, one of the best explosive damage weapons, has also caught a nerf as part of that.

#4521. Bosch’s popular e-bike motor just got upgraded with more power and less weight

Bosch has unveiled the latest generation of its popular Active Line Plus electric bicycle motor, bringing more power, less weight, and a significantly smaller footprint to one of the company’s most widely used drive systems.

The new motor is designed primarily for everyday riders, including commuters, recreational cyclists, and those who want a comfortable e-bike that can handle everything from city streets to weekend trail rides.

And while it isn’t Bosch’s most powerful motor, the upgrades are fairly substantial.

The new Active Line Plus now produces up to 600 watts of peak power and 60 Nm of torque, along with a maximum pedal assistance level of 340%. That’s enough to give riders a healthy boost when accelerating away from traffic lights or climbing hills, without necessarily turning their everyday commuter into an overpowered mountain bike.

Like its predecessor, the motor is designed for Class 1 electric bicycles in the US, providing pedal assistance up to 20 mph (32 km/h) without a throttle.

Remember, the Active Line motor is the drive system model that many e-bike companies use for their modestly performing e-bikes. It gives good power and control, combined with all the tech we’ve come to expect from Bosch, but it isn’t the motor e-bike makers use when they need an electric mountain bike to scale a steep mountainous trail.

Perhaps even more interesting than the increased power is what Bosch has done to the motor’s physical design.

The company developed a new two-stage gearbox that helps reduce the motor’s overall volume by 17% while shaving approximately 1.1 lb (0.5 kg) off its weight.

The new drive unit now tips the scales at around 6 lb (2.7 kg), making it easier for bicycle manufacturers to integrate into slimmer, more traditional-looking frames.

Bosch also says the new gearbox uses specially machined gears to make the motor virtually silent, while updated sensors and software provide smoother, more natural-feeling pedal assistance.

That’s particularly important for a motor like the Active Line Plus, where riders are often looking for an experience that feels like riding a regular bicycle, just with a bit of extra help.

The motor also supports Bosch’s eShift electronic shifting system, which can automatically manage gear changes for riders who prefer to focus on pedaling instead of shifting.

Bosch has additionally improved the motor’s sealing and bearings for better all-weather durability. The housing uses approximately 40% recycled aluminum, helping reduce the carbon footprint of its production.

Trek will be the first North American bicycle brand to introduce the new Active Line Plus motor, installing it on the company’s Marlin+ electric bike.

Bosch also announced several other additions to its e-bike ecosystem, including a new compact LED Controller that’s 65% smaller than its predecessor, an updated ConnectModule with Bluetooth-based theft tracking, and a new 720 Wh PowerTube battery weighing just 8.6 lb (3.9 kg).

There’s also a new Intuvia 200 display, offering a 2.4-inch grayscale screen for riders who prefer a traditional handlebar-mounted display.

While high-performance e-bike motors tend to grab the headlines with increasingly outrageous torque figures, there’s something to be said for improvements to the more practical end of the market – something for the riders looking for convenient and effective transportation instead of peak performance figures.

For the average commuter or recreational rider, a quieter, lighter motor with plenty of usable power is likely to make a bigger difference than squeezing another few dozen Newton-meters out of an already powerful drive system.

And with Bosch’s extensive network of bicycle manufacturing partners, we can expect to see this updated motor making its way into plenty of new electric bikes.

Ever since the Honda Civic Type R HRC Concept appeared at the Tokyo Auto Salon earlier this year, we’ve heard plenty of reports about its future. There have been indications that the hardcore hot hatch is headed for production, along with rumors that it would eventually make its way to the US. However, Honda had never officially confirmed the latter until now.

In a release ahead of this year’s SEMA Show, Honda has confirmed that the Civic Type R HRC Concept is making its North American debut in Las Vegas from November 3 to 6. More importantly, Honda explicitly stated that the model is being developed for the US market.

Sure, this doesn’t mean you’ll be able to stroll into a dealership and drive one home tomorrow (at least not yet), but it’s a big leap from the endless speculation we’ve been hearing. The concept, which first broke cover in Japan, packs in HRC tech and feedback from real racing drivers to push the already sharp Civic Type R even further.

Honda is still keeping the final specs and production dates under wraps, but the Tokyo concept gives us a solid hint at what they’re cooking up.

Rumor has it Honda might drop the HRC-K20C racing engine from the Super Taikyu Series into a street-legal Civic. That could mean more grunt than the standard FL5’s 315 horsepower, but Honda is still playing coy about whether the race-bred engine will actually make the cut.

Visually, the changes are impossible to miss. The concept gets a fresh front end, extra aero bits, flared and vented arches, chunkier side skirts, and a rear diffuser that means business. Top it off with a massive rear wing, Akrapovič exhaust, and HRC-branded cooling gear, and it’s clear this isn’t just a dress-up job.

Earlier reports indicated that HRC is also dialing in upgrades for the suspension, brakes, and cooling to match all that new aero. HRC boss Koji Watanabe has talked about bringing racing tech from Super Taikyu and Super GT into the mix, and it sounds like some aftermarket goodies will be part of the package too.

There’s still a lot up in the air – like just how much power this thing will make, or if Honda will sell it as a full-blown special edition or just offer a bunch of dealer-installed upgrades.

But the Civic Type R HRC Concept isn’t stealing the whole show. Honda’s SEMA booth will be packed with 12 race cars, from the wild new Passport Baja Spec Trophy Truck to a Hasport Prelude Club Racer, Felix Rosenqvist’s 2026 Indy 500-winning IndyCar, and the 2026 Acura ARX-06 GTP prototype.

The Passport Baja Spec is especially wild, packing a 2.4-liter twin-turbo V6 and an 800-volt hybrid setup for over 1,300 horsepower. Honda claims it’ll be the first hybrid Trophy Truck to take on the SCORE World Desert Championship.

HRC is also rolling out its first batch of Performance Parts for Honda and Acura street cars. We’re talking lightweight forged wheels, new exhausts, and a short-throw shifter for the Civic Type R, Integra Type S, and Passport TrailSport. After final testing, these goodies should hit dealerships and the Honda DreamShop in March 2027.

#4519. Tesla Semi catches fire on I-880 with no crash, closes freeway for 10 hours

A Tesla Semi caught fire on Interstate 880 in Hayward, California, on Tuesday evening, and there was no crash. The electric truck’s lithium-ion battery burned long enough to keep the southbound freeway closed for about 10 hours.

The driver got out unhurt. But a Class 8 electric truck catching fire on its own, in traffic, is something Tesla and its growing list of Semi customers need to explain.

The fire broke out at around 5:35 p.m. PT in the southbound lanes near Route 92. CHP Hayward then closed I-880 in both directions, citing “the potential risk of hazardous chemical smoke,” and posted these photos from the scene:

🚨 TRAFFIC ALERT – I-880 FULL CLOSURE 🚨A Tesla semi-truck has caught fire on I-880, resulting in a complete shutdown of both northbound and southbound lanes due to the potential risk of hazardous chemical smoke. pic.twitter.com/O01z32nxpZ

The driver told officers the truck caught fire and that they didn’t know why. No other vehicles were involved.

Northbound reopened Tuesday night. Southbound took much longer. CHP initially warned that the battery could burn for 15 to 18 hours, but crews beat that estimate, and CHP Hayward posted that all lanes were open at around 3:30 a.m. Wednesday.

The CHP photos show firefighters laying foam around the burned-out tractor, with the front of a Premier Trailer Leasing trailer charred behind it. The truck’s operator hasn’t been identified, and Tesla, which doesn’t have a press office, hasn’t commented. The cause is under investigation.

We’ve been here before. In August 2024, a Tesla-operated Semi caught fire on I-80 near Emigrant Gap while driving from Livermore to Tesla’s facility in Sparks, Nevada. At the time, no crash was reported. The NTSB later found the truck had left the road on a curve, hit a delineator post and a tree, and its battery ignited after the impact. Firefighters used about 50,000 gallons of water, and the lanes stayed closed for up to 15 hours.

Hayward is different. Without a crash, the focus shifts to the truck itself: the battery pack, the high-voltage system, the drive units, or something as ordinary as a tire or brake fire that spread.

And the timing isn’t great for Tesla. The company only started volume production of the Semi in Nevada this year, after nearly a decade of delays. WattEV ordered 370 Semis in May, mostly for drayage at the Port of Oakland, just a few miles up I-880 from where Tuesday’s truck burned. In September, Tesla was also named lead supplier on a 2,500-truck ZET SCALE order.

First, some perspective, because this fire is going to get used as an anti-EV talking point. Truck fires are common. According to NFPA data, US fire departments responded to an average of 15,462 large-truck fires per year between 2018 and 2022. That’s about 42 a day, in a fleet that’s overwhelmingly diesel. Mechanical failure was a factor in 44% of them, and only about 2% were tied to a collision.

The same goes for cars. NFPA and DOT data put the US average at one vehicle fire for every 17 million miles traveled, and combustion vehicles make up the vast majority of that fleet. Tesla claims one fire per 140 million miles for its own vehicles. That’s Tesla’s number, but independent data, like government figures we’ve covered before, points the same way: gas vehicles catch fire more often than EVs.

This is not the main reason that pretty much all the other trucks have moved to LFP, but it is still one more reason that looks like a good idea.

Also, designing your own cells is higher risk... at this point, can they even switch supplier?

But that doesn’t get the Semi off the hook. Diesel fires happen across millions of trucks. Tesla doesn’t disclose Semi deliveries, but PepsiCo, its launch customer, was up to about 86 trucks in 2024, and volume production only started a few months ago. With a fleet that small, one fire with no crash is a big data point. It’s also the second Semi fire to shut down a California interstate in about two years.

So we need the cause. If a tire, a brake, or the trailer caught fire and it spread to the tractor, that’s a regular trucking problem. If the pack went into thermal runaway on its own, Tesla needs to find out why before tens of thousands of these trucks hit the road, and fire departments need a better plan than letting a loaded truck burn on a freeway for half the night.

The NTSB investigated the last one. It should look at this one too, and Tesla should publish what it finds. Will it?

#4517. Battlefield 6 may have actually done it: beaten Call of Duty

Battlefield 6 sales are setting all kinds of records, but one in particular has long eluded the Battlefield series.

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

The game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting new series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

The latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

Battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

Battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

November’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

Given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

Mazda is officially pulling the plug on one of the modern automotive industry’s most fascinating engineering experiments. The Japanese automaker is quietly dropping the highly unusual Skyactiv-X engine from the European Mazda3 lineup. As the company streamlines its global powertrain offerings, this change will officially take effect for the upcoming 2027 model year, marking the quiet end of an incredibly ambitious developmental chapter for the brand’s popular compact hatchback.

This innovative 2.0-liter powertrain originally made massive waves across the industry by successfully blending the high-compression, spark-controlled ignition of a diesel with the cleaner emissions of a traditional gasoline engine. Moving forward, overseas hatchback buyers will be restricted to the standard 2.5-liter e-Skyactiv G engine. To help offset the mechanical loss, the 2027 model will feature new interior technology and a premium Homura Plus trim that avoids any base price increases.

For American consumers, this mechanical retirement is largely moot. According to a recent report from Auto Express, despite years of intense speculation and immense hype from automotive enthusiasts, the engine’s U.S. market launch never officially happened. Executive management correctly assumed that domestic buyers would absolutely refuse to pay a premium sticker price for incremental fuel efficiency, especially if it meant sacrificing overall horsepower and passing-lane acceleration on the highway.

Even without this cutting-edge engine on the options list, the brand’s conventional powertrains have proven highly successful in America. Driven by strong consumer demand for reliable, fun-to-drive commuter cars that offer premium interiors at an accessible price point, standard Mazda3 sales jumped 147% recently. This massive growth occurred right as Detroit’s Big Three continued to lose significant ground in the broader compact car segment.

While the complex Skyactiv-X powertrain is disappearing from the hatchback, it will remain available in the European CX-30 crossover for the immediate future. However, its days are undeniably numbered on a global scale. Mazda has already publicly confirmed that both the current “X” and “G” internal combustion engine families will eventually be replaced by an all-new, highly efficient Skyactiv-Z architecture, which is expected to begin rolling out by 2027.

In the meantime, the automaker is aggressively pivoting its powertrain strategy for North America. Rather than relying on ultra-complex internal combustion designs, Mazda is betting on hybrids as it chases another domestic sales record. This strategic shift toward electrified powertrains in larger, premium SUVs is already paying massive dividends, driving Mazda’s impressive sales surge. The Skyactiv-X was a brilliant piece of engineering, but the market has clearly spoken in favor of straightforward hybridization.

#4515. New retro electric motorcycle to debut at EICMA with a novel feature: a second gear

Most electric motorcycles have something in common: a single-speed transmission. But a British company is preparing to shake things up at this year’s EICMA motorcycle show in Milan, where it will unveil a new electric motorcycle demonstrator featuring an unusual two-speed transmission designed to shift gears without interrupting power delivery.

The company behind the technology, E-Motiv Shift Systems, has developed what it calls a seamless powershift transmission, promising improved acceleration, better efficiency, and a more engaging riding experience.

Unlike conventional motorcycle transmissions, which generally require a brief interruption in power during gear changes, E-Motiv’s system is designed to maintain torque throughout the shift.

That could offer some interesting advantages for electric motorcycles, where a lower first gear could provide stronger acceleration while a taller second gear could help optimize motor efficiency at higher speeds.

Of course, most electric motorcycles don’t actually need multiple gears, and very few have ever offered multi-speed transmissions. Electric motors produce strong torque across a wide operating range, which is why manufacturers generally prefer the simplicity, lower weight, and reduced maintenance of single-speed drivetrains.

But that doesn’t mean a second gear couldn’t offer some benefits.

E-Motiv’s technology actually traces its roots back nearly 25 years to the Zeroshift transmission system, which eventually found its way into Aprilia’s MotoGP racing motorcycles in 2015.

It's possible, from my perspective, that running a motor at lower rpm under reduced load like flat terrain cruising, could improve range, and lower temperatures, and might be beneficial for cars and trucks as well.

The latest electric version was developed through a £1 million UK government-funded project involving motorcycle manufacturer BSA, the University of Bath, and the Institute of Advanced Automotive Propulsion Systems (IAAPS).

The demonstrator motorcycle, known as Demo 1, was conceived by British design consultancy Envisage and is being built by IAAPS. Real-world testing is scheduled to begin in early 2027.

E-Motiv will showcase the technology at EICMA from November 3-8, though the demonstrator remains a development project rather than a production-ready motorcycle.

Whether two-speed transmissions eventually become common on electric motorcycles remains to be seen. But if E-Motiv can deliver meaningful efficiency and performance improvements without adding too much weight, cost, or complexity, it could give future electric motorcycles another interesting trick up their sleeves.
